system_description.narrative_title: AI trade unwinds: market rout, safety and geopolitical reckoning
system_description.narrative_summary: The dominant narrative is that the AI investment boom is undergoing a broad reassessment: rising rates, credit/debt worries and doubts about the timing and profitability of enterprise AI are triggering a deep selloff in AI infrastructure, chip and tech stocks. Viewed as an open system, the story links flows of capital, talent, data and regulatory attention between firms, investors, banks and states; negative feedbacks (falling prices → tighter financing → slower deployments → more skepticism) interact with positive stabilizers (safety commitments, corporate pivots, strategic government support), while shocks from energy prices and export-policy shifts enter the system and amplify volatility. The result is simultaneous market repricing, renewed policy intervention on AI and chips, and strategic repositioning by hyperscalers and incumbents.
system_description.scope: Public and private capital flowing into AI and related infrastructure (chipmakers, data centers, cloud hyperscalers, AI startups), investor sentiment and market prices, banks and credit providers financing the AI build-out, corporate product pivots and safety actions, regulators and international trade/policy levers, and supply-chain/energy inputs that affect costs and deployment timelines.
system_description.super_system: Global political-economic system (finance, trade, industrial policy and geopolitical competition)
adjacent_subsystems: Energy, industrial policy & strategic manufacturing (e.g., autos)

variables.name: Investor sentiment toward AI
variables.description: Measures aggregate investor optimism or pessimism about AI-related assets and investment prospects.

variables.name: Capital flow into AI assets
variables.description: Measures the net rate of public and private investment flowing into AI companies, infrastructure and funds.

variables.name: Credit availability for AI build-out
variables.description: Measures the supply and ease of bank and nonbank lending specifically available to finance AI projects and firms.

variables.name: Cost of financing
variables.description: Measures prevailing borrowing costs and interest-rate-related price of capital that affect AI investment decisions.

variables.name: Market prices of AI-related assets
variables.description: Measures valuations and traded prices for equity and other securities tied to AI infrastructure, chipmakers and tech firms.

variables.name: AI deployment rate
variables.description: Measures the pace at which AI systems, data centers and production-grade models are being commissioned and put into operation.

variables.name: Expected AI project profitability
variables.description: Measures market and corporate expectations for return-on-investment and margin outcomes from enterprise AI deployments.

variables.name: Engineering talent allocated to AI
variables.description: Measures the stock of specialized engineers, researchers and technical personnel actively working on AI systems and infrastructure.

variables.name: Data availability and quality
variables.description: Measures the volume, accessibility and labeled quality of datasets available for training, validation and operation of AI models.

variables.name: Regulatory scrutiny of AI
variables.description: Measures the intensity, scope and enforcement pressure of regulatory oversight and compliance requirements affecting AI activities.

variables.name: Export control tightness on AI tech
variables.description: Measures the restrictiveness and practical enforcement of trade and export policies that limit cross-border flows of AI-relevant technologies.

variables.name: Energy price levels
variables.description: Measures prevailing prices and volatility of energy inputs that affect operating costs for data centers and manufacturing.

variables.name: Chip supply capacity
variables.description: Measures production capacity, lead times and throughput for semiconductors and chipmaking equipment needed by AI hardware.

variables.name: AI safety commitment strength
variables.description: Measures the extent to which organizations invest in, implement and publicize safety controls, evaluation and external monitoring for AI systems.

variables.name: Corporate strategic pivot rate
variables.description: Measures the rate at which firms change product roadmaps, business models or investment focus toward or away from AI initiatives.

variables.name: Bank risk tolerance for AI lending
variables.description: Measures banks' willingness to extend credit and accept counterparty and project risk tied to AI investments.

catalysts.title: China draft export controls on AI tech
catalysts.description: Beijing's draft export controls and tightening on AI technologies are likely to restrict cross-border flows of chips and tools, affecting supply and investor confidence.
catalysts.rationale: Driven by headlines: "China unveils draft export controls on AI technologies" and "Beijing seeks tighter grip on AI exports."

catalysts.title: G7 simulated AI attacks on banks
catalysts.description: Planned G7 exercises simulating AI-driven attacks on banks will raise focus on systemic cyber risk, prompting regulatory and sector-level responses.
catalysts.rationale: Based on: "G7 economies plan simulated AI attacks on banks" and "G7 to launch exercises to guard against AI cyber attacks."

catalysts.title: Banks tighten AI agent access and controls
catalysts.description: Banks restricting AI agents from accessing customer accounts and tightening policies will likely lower bank willingness to underwrite AI risk and credit for AI firms.
catalysts.rationale: Cited by: "Citi becomes latest US bank to restrict AI agents" and "Big banks see risks in financing the AI boom."

catalysts.title: Major tech earnings season
catalysts.description: Earnings and guidance from major AI-exposed firms (Microsoft, Shopify, Nvidia-linked suppliers) will drive market re-pricing of AI expectations and valuations.
catalysts.rationale: Headline drivers: "Microsoft, Shopify and 3 more AI stocks that are favorite Wall Street earnings plays" and broader earnings coverage.

catalysts.title: Soaring energy prices pressure data-centers
catalysts.description: Rising energy costs in Europe and globally will increase operating costs for data centres, pressuring AI deployment economics and valuations.
catalysts.rationale: From: "Soaring energy prices set to swamp EU summit" and data-centre cost pressure in AI infrastructure sell-off headlines.

catalysts.title: Chip equipment export negotiations and limits
catalysts.description: Negotiations and conditionalities around chip-equipment exports (SK Hynix, US rules, ASML demand) will shape supply capacity and lead times for AI hardware.
catalysts.rationale: Based on: "SK Hynix conditions new US factory on more US chip equipment exports to China" and related chip export headlines.

catalysts.title: Industry safety pushes and legislative efforts
catalysts.description: Anthropic's push for a safety bill, outside evaluator access, and watchdog calls will accelerate regulatory proposals and corporate safety investments.
catalysts.rationale: Supported by: "Anthropic quietly pitches its own AI safety bill" and "Anthropic grants outside evaluator METR access."

catalysts.title: Capital rotation out of AI into defensive sectors
catalysts.description: Ongoing sell-off is driving reallocations to defensive sectors (big pharma, energy), reducing flows into AI assets and pressuring valuations.
catalysts.rationale: From: "Investors are dumping AI stocks" and "Big pharma stocks close near all-time highs as tech selloff pushes investors toward safer bets."
